sanity_multiples_memo: At A$16.75 and USD/AUD 1.4055 the market cap is ~US$36.7bn (A$51.5bn); EV ~US$37.5bn. FY2026 underlying EBITDA 8,635 gives EV/EBITDA 4.3x; on the base-case mid-cycle EBITDA (~46% x ~US$16bn = ~US$7.4bn) 5.1x. P/B 1.8x on equity 20,245; P/E ~10.6x on underlying NPAT 3,458; owner-FCF yield 9.4% on FY2026's 3,460 but ~5.8% on the FY27 component build (~US$2.1bn) after the capex step-up. Fortescue has traded at 3-6x EV/EBITDA for a decade; the model's 10x owner-FCF terminal cap is roughly 5x mid-cycle EBITDA.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle nominal revenue growth for a ~200Mtpa iron ore producer whose volume is flat (Pilbara hematite ~190Mt sustained, Iron Bridge ramp offsets grade decline) and whose price is assumed to mean-revert; no historical CAGR is usable because every window's endpoints sit at different points of the iron ore price cycle (FY2021 = US$135/dmt peak, FY2016 = US$45/dmt trough)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (+2.7%) diverges >30% from revenue (-5.3% 5yr) and EPS (-22.5% 5yr). The divergence is cycle position, not a data error: FY2021 was the China-stimulus price peak (realised US$135/dmt, NPAT US$10.3bn), and equity grew only 2.7%/yr despite US$21bn of cumulative earnings because ~US$20bn was paid out as dividends. Ten-year revenue CAGR of +9.1% is equally a trough-to-mid artefact (FY2016 realised ~US$45/dmt).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are computed on reported FCF minus SBC (interest income not stripped, the company is in net debt): FY2021 9,118 -> FY2026 3,460 (-17.6%/yr), FY2023 4,383 -> 3,460 (-7.6%/yr). They describe the iron ore price falling from US$135 to US$91/dmt and capex rising from US$3.4bn to US$3.2bn on a much lower revenue base, not a growth trend. SBC (0.0% to 1.15% of revenue) is small enough that the owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs differ by under 1pp; SBC has grown from US$16m to US$195m over the decade, faster than any cash line, but remains immaterial to value. The 11-year owner-FCF series FY2016-FY2026 (US$m): 2,666, 3,511, 686, 3,304, 4,429, 9,118, 3,715, 4,383, 4,929, 3,027, 3,460 -- median 3,511, mean 3,930 -- is the sanity anchor for the base-case mid-cycle owner FCF of ~US$2.6-2.9bn, which sits BELOW the historical median because FY27+ capex (US$3.85-4.85bn guided) and C1 cost (US$20.50-21.75/wmt) are both structurally higher than the decade that produced that median.

scenario_narratives.base: Fortescue's earnings are a function of one price, the Platts 62% Fe iron ore index, applied to a ~190Mt hematite business whose cost base has just stepped up (C1 guided to US$20.50-21.75/wmt for FY27 against US$13.93 in FY2021) and whose capex is guided to US$3.85-4.85bn in FY27, a third above FY2026. The base case takes FY27 at the company's guidance with the realised price held at FY2026's US$91/dmt, then lets pricing fade to ~US$80/dmt over FY28-29 as Simandou's first ~60-120Mtpa enters a flat-to-declining Chinese steel market, and holds a 46% pre-SBC margin at mid-cycle. Capex normalises to ~20% of revenue (~US$3.2bn) once the Real Zero decarbonisation program completes around FY2031, which is what lifts owner FCF from ~US$2.1bn in FY27 back to ~US$2.6-2.9bn, below the decade median of US$3.5bn because both C1 and sustaining capex are structurally higher than the years that produced that median. The axes are the iron ore price path under Simandou supply, the C1 cost trajectory, Iron Bridge's ramp (impaired ~US$750m in FY2026 after the ramp-up was extended), and whether the Energy segment is contained at the guided ~US$300m net cost or resumes multi-billion green-hydrogen spending.
scenario_narratives.bull: Chinese steel output plateaus rather than declines, India's steel build-out absorbs new seaborne supply, and Simandou displaces high-cost Chinese domestic concentrate instead of Pilbara fines, so the index holds ~US$105 and Fortescue realises the low-90s with an improving product mix as Iron Bridge reaches 22Mtpa nameplate at a premium magnetite price. The autonomous, increasingly electrified fleet and cheap Pilbara solar and wind hold C1 near US$20/wmt, the Energy segment is cut to break-even and Fortescue Zero's battery-electric haulage and electrolyser technology is sold to third parties. A 52% pre-SBC margin (the FY2025-26 level) on ~2.5-3% nominal revenue growth, capex falling to 18% of revenue after 2030, and dividends at 65% of NPAT continuing.
scenario_narratives.bear: Simandou reaches ~120Mtpa by FY2029 just as Chinese crude steel falls toward 850-900Mt on the property downturn and rising scrap use; the index settles ~US$75 and, because Fortescue sells the lowest-grade product among the majors, its discount widens and the realised price falls to ~US$62/dmt, a revenue decline of ~22% over three years. C1 rises above US$22/wmt on strip ratios and diesel, Iron Bridge stalls and is impaired again, the Energy segment keeps consuming ~US$500m/yr because the hydrogen projects are neither built nor cleanly exited, and native-title compensation claims follow the US$104m Yindjibarndi award. A 36% pre-SBC margin, below any year on record, with capex stuck at 22-27% of revenue: owner FCF falls to ~US$0.6bn in FY2029 and recovers only to ~US$1.2bn, and the dividend is cut hard. The balance sheet (net debt US$0.9bn, gross gearing 23%) survives; the equity value does not.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A single-commodity iron ore producer is worth its mid-cycle owner cash flow at a mid-cycle cost base, not its best year (FY2021, US$135/dmt, US$9.1bn owner FCF) and not its most recent year (FY2026, US$91/dmt, US$3.5bn owner FCF, but at a C1 cost and capex level that FY27 guidance has already moved higher). The model builds each year from components (revenue x pre-SBC underlying EBITDA margin - SBC - D&A - 31% cash tax + D&A - capex incl. leased-fleet renewal - working capital), anchors FY27 to the company's own guidance (shipments 197-207Mt, C1 US$20.50-21.75/wmt, capex US$3.85-4.85bn, Energy net cost ~US$300m), and fades the realised price to ~US$80/dmt as Simandou supply arrives. It charges leases once (as debt, net debt 857 ties to the company's own figure), SBC once (expensed at 1.15% of revenue against a flat 3,082m diluted count that the employee share trust actually funds), and risk once (in the scenario flows and a 30% bear weight, at a single 9.5% USD WACC). The terminal value is capped at 10x owner FCF (~5x mid-cycle EBITDA) because the market has never paid more than ~6x EBITDA for Fortescue. All values are computed in USD and converted to AUD at 1.4055 for comparison with the ASX price.
key_risks_to_valuation: Iron ore price path: each US$10/dmt on realised price is ~US$1.75bn of revenue and roughly A$3-4/share of value; the base case's US$80/dmt mid-cycle is a judgment about Simandou supply against Chinese steel demand, and the 62% index has averaged ~US$100-110 over the past decade

Cost base: FY27 C1 guidance of US$20.50-21.75/wmt is up 51% on FY2021's US$13.93; each US$1/wmt is ~US$190m of EBITDA (~1.1pp of margin). Strip ratios (1.62x in FY2026) are rising as Chichester and Solomon hubs mature

Capex normalisation: the valuation depends on capex falling from ~26% of revenue (FY27 guidance) to ~20% by FY2032 as the Real Zero decarbonisation program (US$0.9-1.3bn/yr) completes; a new wave of green-hydrogen or downstream (green iron) capital would defer the FCF harvest

Iron Bridge: extended ramp-up (FY27 guidance 11-14Mt vs 22Mtpa nameplate), ~US$750m impaired in FY2026; a further impairment or a decision to run below nameplate removes the premium-product mix improvement the bull case relies on

Fortescue Energy: the segment lost US$422m at the EBITDA line in FY2026 and US$741m in FY2025; the model assumes the guided ~US$300m net cost holds, not the multi-billion hydrogen program of 2022-2024. Founder control (Dr Andrew Forrest ~37%) means the capital allocation risk is idiosyncratic, in both directions

China concentration and grade: ~85-90% of sales to Chinese mills, and Fortescue's 56-58% Fe product carries the widest discount among the majors; discounts widen in a buyer's market, which is why the bear case realises US$62/dmt on a US$75 index
Native title and legal: the US$104m Yindjibarndi compensation in FY2026 is a precedent for further claims across the Pilbara tenements

FX: AUD-denominated costs (~70% of C1) against USD revenue; management guides on AUD:USD 0.70 and each cent moves C1 by ~US$0.16/wmt. The AUD quote also moves the AUD-denominated IV one-for-one with the USD/AUD rate even when the USD valuation is unchanged
Dividend policy (50-80% of NPAT, FY2026 65%) means the company retains little cushion; the bear case implies a dividend cut of more than half from the FY2026 A$1.08/share

data_sources.financials: research/FMG.AX/Reports/FMG.AX_Metrics.csv (core_metrics + kpis, FY2016-FY2026 annual and half-year, USD millions) and FMG.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt for FY27 guidance (lines 1728-1751), diluted shares (lines 12600-12610), borrowings and leases (lines 2653-2660), segment underlying EBITDA (line 2161), realised prices (lines 2089-2092), cash-flow financing lines incl. lease repayment and employee share trust purchases (lines 12170-12180), SBC (line 12905)
data_sources.qualitative: FMG.AX_Analysis.json was not present at build time; bull/bear axes drawn from the FY2026 Annual Report operating and financial review, outlook, segment note and Iron Bridge impairment note (line 13581)

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average 3,082,121,195 (FY2026 AR note, EPS denominator: 3,076,300,671 basic + 5,820,524 potential ordinary shares from share rights) held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows. Fortescue satisfies share rights through on-market purchases by the employee share trust (US$157m in FY2026, US$163m in FY2025, financing activities), so the flat count is genuinely funded; buyback_cash records that trust purchase. No formal buyback program.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report statement of changes in equity 'Share-based payment expense' 195 (line 12905; FY2025 184 at FY2025 AR line 15245). No separate equity-award tax line is disclosed and no combined figure is published; awards are settled from the employee share trust so there is no net-share-settlement tax outflow to add.
inputs.buyback_note: Not a buyback program: 'Purchase of shares by employee share trust' (157) in FY2026 financing activities, the cash that funds share rights and keeps the count flat. ShareRepurchases KPI is 0 in every period.
inputs.fx_note: Statements, flows and every driver are in US dollars (Fortescue reports in US$m; dividends are declared in AUD cents and stored separately as the DividendPerShareAUD KPI). The ASX quote is AUD. All per-share values are computed in USD then converted at USD/AUD 1.4055 = 1 / 0.7115 (Yahoo AUDUSD=X regularMarketPrice 0.7115 at 2026-09-22T11:28:06Z). Parity check: no dual listing trades in USD (the OTC ADR FSUGY is 1:1 but illiquid), so the check is against guidance instead: management's FY27 guidance assumes AUD:USD 0.70, within 2% of the rate used. The unsuffixed intrinsic values and weighted_iv are in AUD (the quote currency) so they compare directly to current_price; the USD twins are the model-currency basis.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-22T06:12:33Z (ASX regular close, 16:12 AEST; Yahoo chart meta, marketState not reported)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD-built, because the flows are USD (iron ore is priced in USD, the debt is USD senior notes and term loans, the statements are US$m): US 10-year Treasury ~4.2% risk-free, 5.0% equity risk premium, equity beta ~1.2 for a single-commodity iron ore producer gives a cost of equity of ~10.2%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.8% on Baa1/BBB+ senior unsecured notes and term loans, ~4.1% after 30% tax; weights ~86% equity / 14% debt at market value (market cap ~US$36.7bn at the AUD price and 0.7115, gross debt US$5.9bn) give 9.35%, rounded to 9.5%. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios. Single-commodity exposure, China customer concentration (~85-90% of sales) and the Simandou supply wave are charged ONCE, in the scenario flows and the 30% bear weight, not stacked into the discount rate (adaptations section f). Step 8c.5 of the research-stock skill would allow a +1.5-2.5% single-customer premium and +1-2% cyclicality premium if the sanity check trips on WACC; they have not been pre-applied.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt. Lease liabilities of 629 (FY2026 AR line 2655: 604 in FY2025) are INCLUDED in total_debt (borrowings 5,302 at line 2653 + leases 629 = 5,931) and hence in net_debt: 5,931 - cash 5,074 = 857, which ties exactly to the company's reported 'Net debt 857' (lines 2660, 12646). Lease principal ('Repayment of leases' 150 in FY2026 financing, 406 in FY2025 which included a large one-off) is therefore NOT deducted from the flows and last_fcf = OCF 6,836 - capex 3,181 - SBC 195 = 3,460 with no lease deduction. Ongoing renewal of the leased asset base (mining fleet, port and rail equipment, vessels) is charged as a capex-like line: ~0.9% of revenue (150 / 16,966 = 0.88%) is folded into every year of capex_pct_path, so the leased fleet is neither free nor double-charged. D&A already includes right-of-use depreciation and is left as reported because under treatment (A) the lease is a financed asset like any other.
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial and not separately charged. Non-controlling interests took 10 of FY2026 profit (line 12040; 7 in FY2025) and the NCI stock is 38 (line 12131), 0.2% of equity. FY2026 NPAT attributable 2,860 vs total 2,870. Iron Bridge (69% Fortescue / 31% Formosa) is a joint operation, consolidated at Fortescue's 69% share of assets, revenue and costs, so no NCI arises there. The 10/yr of leakage is inside the 31% cash-tax rate's rounding.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted, with the section 7 cyclical/non-US adaptations (USD flows vs AUD quote, leases as debt, risk charged once), on a MID-CYCLE basis. Fortescue is an operating company (Pilbara hematite iron ore ~190Mt/yr, Iron Bridge magnetite ramping to 22Mtpa on a 100% basis, plus the loss-making Fortescue Energy / Fortescue Zero segment), so the owner-FCF engine is the right family; the adaptation is that no single year is a repeatable base: FY2021 (US$135/dmt realised, 74% pre-SBC margin, US$9.1bn owner FCF) was the China-stimulus peak, FY2016/FY2018 (45-46% margins on US$45-55/dmt realised) were troughs, and FY2026 (US$91/dmt, 52.0% pre-SBC underlying margin, owner FCF US$3.46bn) sits near the middle of the price range but at a C1 cost (US$18.74/wmt) that is guided UP to US$20.50-21.75/wmt in FY27 and BEFORE the FY27 capex step-up to US$3.85-4.85bn (Metals US$3.7-4.7bn incl. decarbonisation US$0.9-1.3bn, plus Energy ~US$150m). EBITDA MARGIN BASIS: the engine's ebitda_margin_path is PRE-SBC (before the SBC charge the engine deducts) and is anchored to UNDERLYING EBITDA, not statutory: FY2026 statutory EBITDA 7,384 is after a ~US$750m pre-tax impairment (Iron Bridge ramp-up deferral, non-cash), US$104m Yindjibarndi compensation (cash, one-off) and other significant items; underlying 8,635 + SBC 195 = 8,830 / 16,966 = 52.0%. Segment: Metals 9,082 (54% margin), Energy (422), Other (25). MID-CYCLE JUDGMENT: the 11-year pre-SBC underlying margin record is median 59.6% / mean 57.6%, but that record was earned at C1 costs of US$13-18/wmt and a Platts 62% index averaging ~US$100-110/dmt. The base case does not use it. It assumes realised hematite pricing fades from US$91/dmt to ~US$80/dmt over FY28-FY29 as Simandou (Rio/Chinalco/WCS, first ore CY2026, ~120Mtpa at full rate) enters a Chinese steel market that is flat to declining, with C1 at US$21/wmt and the Energy segment's net operating cost cut to the guided ~US$300m: Metals EBITDA of ~US$38/dmt against the FY22-FY24 60-65 shown in the report's own through-cycle chart, a group pre-SBC margin of 46%. INTEREST INCOME: NOT stripped (interest_income = 0 in the deduction) because the company is in net debt (US$857m); the 180 of finance income (line 2167) is left in the flows and the US$5.07bn cash is netted in the bridge at face. No matching-asset issue arises. LAST_FCF: 3,460 = reported FCF 3,655 (OCF 6,836 - capex 3,181, capex being Fortescue PP&E 3,033 + joint-operations PP&E 148, lines 12157/12163) - SBC 195 - interest income 0. CASH TAX: 31% flat, modelled cash rate. FY2026 income tax expense 1,477 was a 34.1% ETR (line 2588) inflated by non-deductible impairment and unrecognised Energy losses; cash tax paid 1,821 (line 12152) was 42% of PBT 4,337 because Australian instalments lag the prior, higher-profit year. The Australian statutory 30% plus ~1pp of non-deductible Energy/overseas leakage is the repeatable rate; no NOL or credit is being perpetuated. ANALYSIS JSON: research/FMG.AX/Reports/FMG.AX_Analysis.json did not exist when this file was written (qualitative-analyst runs in parallel); the bull/bear axes below are drawn from the FY2026 annual report (outlook, segment note, impairment note) and the KPI history. PRICE: ASX regular-close print; not an after-hours quote.

bear.margin_note: Simandou reaches its ~120Mtpa run-rate by FY2029 into a Chinese steel market shrinking toward 850-900Mt as property completions keep falling and scrap-based EAF share rises; the Platts 62% index settles ~US$75 and the discount on Fortescue's lower-grade (56-58% Fe) hematite widens in a buyer's market to a realised ~US$62/dmt. C1 drifts above US$22/wmt on strip ratios (1.62x in FY2026 and rising) and diesel; Iron Bridge stalls below 15Mtpa with further impairment; Energy keeps burning ~US$500m/yr because the green-hydrogen projects are neither built nor cleanly wound down; further native-title compensation (Yindjibarndi) crystallises. Pre-SBC margin 36%, well below any year in the record, because the FY2016-18 trough margins were earned at a C1 of US$13-15/wmt. Capex stays elevated for longer on decarbonisation commitments and Iron Bridge remediation.

base.growth_note: FY2027 flat: shipments guided 197-207Mt (midpoint 202 vs 201.3 actual) at a realised hematite price held at the FY2026 US$91/dmt, with Iron Bridge 11-14Mt (100% basis) at ~US$120/dmt adding little at Fortescue's 69% share. FY2028 -5% and FY2029 -4% as Simandou volumes reach the market and realised pricing fades to ~US$80/dmt (a ~US$92-95 Platts 62% index at Fortescue's ~86% realisation). +2% nominal thereafter: flat hematite volume, Iron Bridge ramp offsetting grade decline, price inflation.
base.margin_note: Pre-SBC, underlying basis (FY2026 = 52.0%). FY2027 50.0%: the FY27 C1 guidance of US$20.50-21.75/wmt (midpoint 21.1 vs 18.74 actual) costs ~US$450m on ~190Mt of hematite (-2.6pp), partly offset by the Energy segment's net operating cost falling from the FY2026 US$422m loss to the guided ~US$300m (+0.7pp), less Iron Bridge dilution. Fades to a 46% mid-cycle by FY2029 on US$80/dmt realised: Metals EBITDA of ~US$38/dmt after C1 US$21, royalties ~7.5% of revenue, shipping ~US$8/wmt and the Energy drag, versus the US$60-65/dmt the report's own through-cycle chart shows for FY22-FY24 at a US$110-120 index. 46% sits between the FY2016/FY2018 troughs (45-46%, when C1 was US$13-15) and the FY2025-26 level (52%), which is where a permanently higher cost base at a mid-cycle price lands.
base.capex_note: Includes ~0.9pp/yr for leased-asset renewal (treatment A, see inputs.lease_treatment). FY2027 26.5% = guided Metals US$3.7-4.7bn midpoint 4.2bn + Energy ~US$150m = US$4.35bn (25.6%) + 0.9. FY2028 25.5% and FY2029 24.0% as decarbonisation spend (US$0.9-1.3bn/yr toward Real Zero 2030: Cloudbreak/Solomon/Turner River solar, Nullagine wind, BESS, PEC transmission) continues on a shrinking revenue base; then 22.0%, 20.5% and a 20.0% steady state (~US$3.1-3.3bn: sustaining and hub development US$2.3-2.7bn, exploration and studies US$0.3-0.5bn, residual decarbonisation and fleet renewal) once the decarbonisation program completes around FY2031. Steady-state capex 1.5pp above D&A reflects a depleting ore body and replacement-cost inflation.
base.da_note: As reported, including right-of-use depreciation (treatment A). FY2026 D&A 2,872 = 16.9% of revenue and rose 15% y/y as Iron Bridge and decarbonisation assets were commissioned; 17.0% in FY2027 rising to 18.5% as the FY27-FY30 capex program depreciates against a lower mid-cycle revenue base.
base.tax_note: 31% modelled cash rate: Australian 30% statutory plus ~1pp of non-deductible Energy and overseas losses (NCI leakage of ~10/yr is inside the rounding). FY2026 ETR of 34.1% was inflated by the non-deductible impairment; cash tax paid of 42% of PBT was instalment timing. See inputs.notes.
base.wc_note: Iron ore producer with trade receivables and inventories (ore stockpiles, consumables) modestly above payables; -5% capture on the revenue change, so the FY2028-29 revenue fall releases a little cash and later growth consumes a little.
base.terminal_note: 10x owner-FCF cap for a single-commodity producer with a depleting resource and one customer country (Gordon at 9.5%/2.0% would be 13.6x); the cap binds. 10x owner FCF is ~5x mid-cycle EBITDA, the middle of Fortescue's own 3-6x decade range.

bull.margin_note: Chinese steel output stabilises near 1bn tonnes with India and South-East Asia absorbing the growth, Simandou ramps slowly and displaces higher-cost Chinese domestic ore rather than Pilbara fines, the Platts 62% index holds ~US$105 and Fortescue's realisation improves as Iron Bridge concentrate (premium, ~US$120/dmt) reaches its 22Mtpa nameplate; C1 held near US$20/wmt by the autonomous fleet and green-power cost savings; Energy scaled back to break-even with Fortescue Zero technology (battery electric haul trucks, electrolysers) monetised to third parties. Pre-SBC margin 52%, the FY2025-26 level sustained, still 8pp below the 11-year median.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 10x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% default because Fortescue sells one commodity, of the lowest grade among the majors, to essentially one country (~85-90% of revenue to Chinese steel mills), and the supply shock that would compress its realised price is not hypothetical: Simandou's first ore is scheduled for CY2026 and ramps over exactly this model's fade years. This is a single-commodity, single-customer-country dependency on top of ordinary cyclicality. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right at once: Chinese steel demand holding near 1bn tonnes, Simandou displacing domestic rather than Pilbara ore, and Fortescue simultaneously holding C1 near US$20, ramping Iron Bridge to nameplate and containing Energy. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
